_derivations.tick_value_usd: NOT A §12A KNOB — this is not a §12A knob, and §12A names no tick value anywhere. It is an EXCHANGE CONTRACT CONSTANT that §7:476 and §7:501 both require by name: `risk_contracts = floor( per_trade_risk_$ / ((stop_ticks + slippage_pad) × tick_value) )` and `dollar_risk = (stop_ticks + slippage_pad) × tick_value × contracts`. It has no other physical home in the tree: risks/ carries no instrument table, and the live margin/instrument cache that will eventually own these numbers is R3-B/R4 work that does not exist. The KEYS are §7:495's symbol scope ('up to 5 top-liquid (ES, NQ, CL, GC, ZN)') transcribed rather than invented, and boot-validated against the seam's §7:498 bucket membership so a bucketed symbol can never lack a tick value. The NUMBERS are standard CME contract arithmetic (ES 0.25pt x $50, NQ 0.25pt x $20, CL 0.01 x $1000, GC 0.10 x $100, ZN 1/64 x $1000) and are CC-verify placeholders until read off the venue. docs/nix_strategy_contract_v1.1.md:81 makes tick_value informational on the STRATEGY side; that says nothing about the Allocator, which §7:501 requires to compute dollar risk with it.
_derivations.micro_weight: NOT A §12A KNOB — this is not a §12A knob. §7:502-504 states the figure outright in prose rather than as a named tunable: 'Correlation buckets count micros at 1/10 weight' (§7:493) and 'Micros count at 1/10 weight (their dollar risk falls out naturally)' (§7:502). 0.1 is that stated 1/10, unmodified, and it is the one value in this file that is NOT a CC-calibrate placeholder. It is expressed as a knob rather than a literal in code so the §7:502 figure has exactly one physical home, and scripts/tests/test_allocator_caps.py asserts that applying it to a full contract's tick value equals using the micro instrument's own tick value — the 'falls out naturally' equivalence, checked rather than assumed.

_boot_validation.why: Every tick value must be > 0. A zero or negative tick value makes per-contract dollar risk zero or negative, at which point §7:511's inequality admits every size under every ceiling — a cap that cannot bind is not a cap, and it would fail SILENTLY rather than loudly.

The micro weight must lie in (0, 1]. §7:502 makes a micro's dollar risk a FRACTION of a full contract's; a weight above 1 would make micros count for MORE than fulls in a concentration measure, inverting the rule it implements.

Every symbol §7:498 places in a correlation bucket must have a tick value here. The two sets are checked against scripts/nixalloc/seam.py's BUCKET_OF rather than against a list typed in the validator, so a symbol added to a bucket with no tick value is a loud boot failure instead of a cap computed against a number that does not exist.
